note: How long a company can be the only seller of a drug, and where that time goes. Two clocks run at once: the patent, which starts when the molecule is filed, and regulatory exclusivity, which starts at approval and does not depend on holding a patent at all.

exclusivities.name: New chemical entity
exclusivities.what: A brand-new small molecule. No generic application may even be filed for five years

exclusivities.name: Orphan drug
exclusivities.what: A disease affecting fewer than 200,000 Americans. Seven years, and it stacks on the rest

exclusivities.name: New biologic
exclusivities.what: Antibodies and other biologics. Twelve years before a biosimilar can be approved

exclusivities.name: Paediatric study
exclusivities.what: Six months added to whatever is already running, for testing the drug in children

thicket.note: The patent is not the only wall. AbbVie filed 247 patent applications on Humira and was granted 132; an analysis of the US portfolio found about 80% of them were not patentably distinct from one another. Biosimilars reached European patients in 2018 and American patients in 2023.

sources: Patent term, restoration and the 14-year post-approval cap: the Hatch-Waxman Act. Restoration returns up to 5 years lost to FDA review, but total protection after approval cannot exceed 14 years, which is why effective exclusivity lands at 10 to 14 years.

Exclusivity periods: FDA — 5 years for a new chemical entity, 7 for an orphan drug, 12 for a new biologic under the BPCIA, plus 6 months for paediatric studies. These run from approval and are independent of any patent.

Humira: I-MAK analysis of the patent portfolio (247 applications, 132 granted); Journal of Law and the Biosciences, 'Biological patent thickets and delayed access to biosimilars' (2022), which found about 80% of the US patents were not patentably distinct. European biosimilar entry October 2018, US January 2023.
